descripcion_geo: Place in the Valley of Hinnom, south of Jerusalem, where child sacrifices were made to Molech.
importancia_estrategica: Abominable pagan place of worship that prophets identified as a symbol of divine punishment.

historias.titulo: Kings sacrifice their children at Topheth
historias.descripcion: Kings Ahaz and Manasseh put their sons through the fire in the Valley of Hinnom.
In his reform, Josiah desecrates the Tophet of the Valley of Hinnom so that no one can sacrifice their children there again.
Jeremiah prophesies that Topheth will be called 'Valley of Slaughter' because of the imminent punishment on Jerusalem.

personajes.descripcion: He destroyed places of pagan worship, including Topheth, in his great religious reform.
He used the figure of Tophet to announce the judgment on Jerusalem.
He made his sons pass through the fire at Topheth; His reign is the most condemned by the prophets.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Place of religious horror; symbol of Israel apostasy. His name derived from 'Gehenna' (Gehinnom), used in the NT as an image of hell.

judaismo.descripcion: Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom (Ge-Hinnom) was the place of sacrifices by fire; It became a burning garbage dump.
judaismo.significado_teologico: Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom (Ge-Hinnom) was the place of sacrifices by fire; It became a burning garbage dump.

cristianismo.descripcion: Jesus uses 'Gehenna' (Gehinnom) 11 times in the gospels as an image of eternal punishment (Mt 5:22,29,30).
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Jesus uses 'Gehenna' (Gehinnom) 11 times in the gospels as an image of eternal punishment (Mt 5:22,29,30).
